project.name: Fictional Field Desk
project.question: Which follow-through experiment should we prototype next?

method.summary: One simulated analysis using four role lenses and the fictional supplied brief. No people were contacted and no product was inspected.
limitations: All example businesses, workflows and claims are fictional.
Four represented perspectives are not four independent reviews or interviews.
No measured demand, usability improvement or buying intent is available.

evidence.claim: The fictional brief describes a job list, an assignment step and a Complete button; it does not establish that physical work is verified.
evidence.source: Fictional example brief supplied for this template

reviewers.job: Identify jobs awaiting information or follow-up.
reviewers.objection: Another board could duplicate the current job list.
reviewers.disconfirming_question: On the last job, what could the existing list not tell you?

reviewers.job: Assess workload and whether new software reduces administration.
reviewers.incentive: Potentially less checking and predictable cost.
reviewers.objection: No savings are established; staff may need to maintain two systems.
reviewers.disconfirming_question: Would preparation and checking take less time than your existing method?

reviewers.job: Receive the relevant instructions for one job.
reviewers.objection: May prefer a message or export rather than another account.
reviewers.disconfirming_question: Would this replace a repeated call, or merely add a login?

reviewers.job: Understand the next question and reported progress.
reviewers.objection: A polished update could imply completion that no one confirmed.
reviewers.disconfirming_question: Which status actually helped you decide what to do next?

needs.need: See what remains unresolved after assignment.
needs.uncertainty: The current list may already support this.

needs.need: Give the next person relevant instructions and questions.
needs.uncertainty: A separate workspace may be unnecessary.

candidates.name: Unresolved-work review
candidates.rationale: Tests whether separating assigned, reported and reviewed states reduces checking.
candidates.human_decision: Coordinator chooses the next action; generation never completes a job.
candidates.dissent: The existing job list may suffice; compare preparation and checking effort.

experiment_design.phase: Proposed future comparison only; no test has been run.
experiment_design.comparison: Replay a recent anonymized job using current tools and the proposed checklist.
experiment_design.decision_rule: Continue only if the checklist reduces combined work without hiding unknowns.

candidates.name: Scoped handoff preview
candidates.rationale: Try a smaller addition to the existing message/export flow.
candidates.human_decision: Operator reviews the audience and text; saving does not send.
candidates.dissent: Recipient may not need a product account at all.

disagreements.issue: Does the receiving technician need a workspace?

positions.position: A shared view might reduce repeated status checks.
A short message or export may be sufficient.

disagreements.resolution: Prototype a scoped handoff within the existing flow before proposing another portal.
disagreements.uncertainty: No real receiving provider has evaluated the artifact.

next_validation: Compare one anonymized recent job using current tools versus the prototype.
Record preparation time, checking effort, errors and repeated entry; ask the recipient whether the output helps.

checks.name: Product interaction review
checks.detail: This is a fictional format example, not a tested product.

unknowns: Actual fields and enforcement have not been inspected.
The frequency and cost of follow-up remain unknown.

records: Job J-42 has a recorded staff assignment.
A required customer detail is still blank.
scenarios.review: Assignment does not establish the missing detail or attendance. Check whether the existing list/export already exposes these questions.
